module.purpose: Defines the hierarchical state-machine node used by the editor to model tools, child states, transitions, event dispatch, lifecycle hooks, and active-state observability.
module.summary: This file implements the core hierarchical editor state abstraction. Nodes can be roots, branches, or leaves; branches construct and activate child nodes, transitions navigate dotted child paths, lifecycle hooks manage activation and deactivation, and events propagate from the active node down the hierarchy. Reactive atoms and computed values expose active state and paths, while optional performance tracking integrates state transitions with editor interaction metrics.
module.businessContext: Supports editor interaction tools and their nested modes. If state transitions or event propagation fail, editor tools can become stuck, misreport their active mode, or lose interaction lifecycle events.

typeShapes.name: TLStateNodeConstructor
typeShapes.shape:
export interface TLStateNodeConstructor {
	new (editor: Editor, parent?: StateNode): StateNode
	id: string
	initial?: string
	children?(): TLStateNodeConstructor[]
	isLockable: boolean
	useCoalescedEvents: boolean
	trackPerformance: boolean
}

moduleContractTests.then: node.getIsActive() === true && node.getCurrent() === childState && childState.getIsActive() === true
moduleContractTests.rationale: Branch entry must activate its configured initial descendant.

moduleContractTests.scenario: An active node receives an event while its current child remains unchanged.
moduleContractTests.then: the node handler and childState.handleEvent(info) are invoked
moduleContractTests.rationale: Events must propagate through the active state path.

moduleContractTests.scenario: A node handler transitions away from the child that was current when dispatch began.
moduleContractTests.then: childA.handleEvent(info) is not invoked when node.getCurrent() !== childA
moduleContractTests.rationale: Dispatch must avoid sending an event to a child exited during the parent handler.
Exiting a node must deactivate its active descendant.

moduleContractTests.scenario: A child is added to a leaf node.
moduleContractTests.then: throws Error('StateNode.addChild: cannot add child to a leaf node')
moduleContractTests.rationale: Leaf nodes cannot be converted into containers through dynamic child registration.

moduleContractTests.scenario: A child constructor creates an identifier already registered on the node.
moduleContractTests.then: throws Error(`StateNode.addChild: a child with id 'child' already exists`)
moduleContractTests.rationale: Child identifiers must remain unique within a state node.

units.name: StateNode

detail.name: StateNode
detail.signature: export abstract class StateNode implements Partial<TLEventHandlers>
detail.summary: StateNode defines the abstract state-tree node shape used by editor tools, including node identity, hierarchy, active-child tracking, and configurable state behavior.

units.name: constructor

detail.name: constructor
preconditions: The concrete StateNode constructor may provide static id, children, initial, isLockable, and useCoalescedEvents configuration.
postconditions: parent references the provided parent, or an empty fallback object when no parent is provided.
id is copied from the concrete constructor configuration.
_isActive is initialized as a false atom named 'toolIsActive' plus the node id.
_current is initialized as an undefined atom named 'toolState' plus the node id.
_path is initialized as a computed value based on this node id and the current descendant path.
isLockable and useCoalescedEvents are assigned from the concrete constructor configuration.
performanceTracker is initialized with a new PerformanceTracker.
If children and initial are both configured, child instances are created with this editor and this node as their parent, stored by child id, and the configured initial child is selected.
invariants: A node with no parent has type 'root'.
A node with a parent has type 'branch' only when both children and initial are configured; otherwise it has type 'leaf'.
Every child constructed by this unit receives the same editor and the newly constructed node as its parent.
The current child, when selected, is one of the entries created from the configured child constructors.
edgeCases: When parent is omitted, parent is set to an empty fallback object and the node is classified as 'root'.
When a parent is provided without both children and initial configuration, no child instances are created and the node is classified as 'leaf'.
When children and initial are configured on a parentless node, the node is classified as 'root' and its configured initial child is selected.
When children and initial are configured on a node with a parent, the node is classified as 'branch' and its configured initial child is selected.
When the configured initial id does not match a constructed child id, the current child is set to undefined rather than being validated or replaced.

errorPolicy.onInvalidInput: No explicit input validation is performed; failures from child construction, reactive primitive creation, or PerformanceTracker construction propagate.

stateMutations: Initializes editor, parent, id, type, initial, children, isLockable, useCoalescedEvents, and performanceTracker on the new StateNode instance.
Initializes and updates the _isActive, _current, and _path reactive state holders.
Constructs and stores configured child StateNode instances in children.
detail.summary: Initializes a state node with its editor, hierarchy role, reactive state holders, configuration flags, and performance tracker. When the node configuration declares children and an initial child, it constructs those children and selects the configured initial child.

specLiterals.role: Prefix used to name the node's active-state atom.
Prefix used to name the node's current-child atom.
Prefix used to name the node's computed path.
Type assigned to a node constructed without a parent.
Type assigned to a parented node with configured children and an initial child.
Type assigned to a parented node without both configured children and an initial child.

specTests.when: Construct the node without a parent.
specTests.then: The node has type 'root', creates both child nodes with itself as their parent, and selects child 'a' as its current child.

specTests.when: Construct the node with a parent.
specTests.then: The node has type 'leaf' and does not create or select child nodes.

units.name: transition

detail.name: transition
preconditions: id is a string representing a child-state path.
Each path segment intended for traversal identifies a child state of the current state node.
postconditions: The active child-state hierarchy is transitioned according to the dot-separated segments in id.
The supplied transition info is available to the relevant enter and exit lifecycle handlers.
invariants: Path segments are interpreted from left to right.
The transition operates relative to the StateNode on which it is invoked.
edgeCases: A dotted id is split into multiple path segments and traversed as a nested child-state path.
When info is omitted, the method uses an empty object as the transition information.
stateMutations: Updates the current-child state held by the traversed StateNode instances.
detail.summary: Transitions this state node through the dot-separated child-state path identified by id. The supplied info object is passed to the transition lifecycle handlers.

specLiterals.role: Delimiter separating nested child-state identifiers in the transition path.

units.name: handleEvent

detail.name: handleEvent
preconditions: The referenced current and target child state identifiers are available to the handler.
The state node's child-state collection can resolve the requested target identifier.
postconditions: When the target child differs from the previous child, the previous active child is exited before the target child is entered.
The current-child reference is updated to the target child before entering it.
The target child is entered with the previous child identifier, or "initial" when no previous child exists.
invariants: A missing target child causes an error rather than entering or selecting an undefined child.
A previously selected child is exited only when it is currently active.
The target child is not re-entered when its identifier matches the previous child identifier.
edgeCases: If no child exists for the requested identifier, an Error is thrown with the current state identifier and requested identifier.
If there is no previous child, the target child is entered with the source identifier "initial".
If the previous child exists but is inactive, it is not exited again.
If the previous and target child identifiers are equal, the child reference is not changed and no enter or exit is performed.
If the entered target child is inactive, processing stops after entry.

errorPolicy.onInvalidInput: Throws when the requested child state cannot be found.

stateMutations: The current child reference is updated to the resolved target child.
The previous active child may be exited.
The target child may be entered.
detail.summary: Handles a state event by resolving the target child state and updating the active child when the target differs from the current child. It exits the previously active child when necessary and enters the target child.

specLiterals.value: ${currState.id} - no child state exists with the id ${id}.
specLiterals.role: Error message thrown when the requested child state cannot be resolved.
Fallback identifier supplied when entering a target child without a previous child.

units.name: enter

detail.name: enter
edgeCases: Performance instrumentation is considered only when the node constructor's trackPerformance setting is enabled.
When debugFlags.measurePerformance is disabled, the performance-measurement branch is not taken.
detail.summary: Enters this state node using the supplied event information and source-state identifier. When performance tracking is enabled, entry processing is subject to the configured performance instrumentation path.

units.name: exit

detail.name: exit
detail.summary: Defines the operation used to exit a StateNode and complete its state transition lifecycle.

units.name: addChild

detail.name: addChild
preconditions: The child argument is a StateNode instance with a usable state-node identity.
postconditions: The child is present in this node's child collection under its identity.
The method returns the same child instance supplied by the caller.
invariants: Child lookup is keyed by the child's state-node identity.
Adding a child does not alter the child instance itself.
edgeCases: Adding a child whose identity already exists replaces the existing entry for that identity.
The supplied child remains the returned value regardless of whether its identity was already present.
stateMutations: This node's child collection is updated with the supplied child, keyed by the child's identity.
detail.summary: Adds a child state node to this node's child collection, keyed by the child's identity, and returns the added child.

specTests.when: addChild is called with the child.
specTests.then: The child can be found in the parent's child collection under its identity, and the returned value is the exact child instance supplied.
